messages:
maria-recruiter: Morning \u2014 ran into a weird one after the overnight ATS bulk import. A handful of candidate attachments are showing as 0 bytes in the UI. Noticed during packet review. :grimacing:

maria-recruiter: Job id 778, ~3.8k rows, affected about 22 attachments (~0.6%). Originals were ~500KB-2MB.

jamie-atsbot: job 778 status: COMPLETED with warnings. Detected 22 attachments with E_UPLOAD_TRUNCATED from putAttachment(). Runbook: https://docs/internal/ats/runbooks#E_UPLOAD_TRUNCATED

alex-ops: Thanks. Quick triage  are the zero-byte objects present in staging or only after the ATS move?

maria-recruiter: Staging copies look fine on a quick sample. Zero-bytes appear after the post-import move into service storage.

leo-eng: Pulling post-process logs for the window. Found repeated proxy 499/timeouts during attachment write: "proxy: upstream returned 499 while reading response header" and lines showing 0 bytes written. That lines up with the symptom.

leo-eng: Looks like our post-processing currently marks the attachment as stored even when the proxy aborts mid-stream. We should add a checksum verify before flipping the saved flag.

alex-ops: Agreed. Immediate plan: 1) ops rehydrate affected attachments from staging, verify checksums; 2) eng add checksum verification + extra retry on proxy abort. Sarah can coordinate comms.

sarah-peopleops: I'll prepare a short note to recruiters once we have the rehydrate results and candidate list. Prioritize candidates with interviews tomorrow.

alex-ops: Running a dry-run list now: ./tools/ats_rehydrate --manifest import-20260410-778.json --dry-run 
Found 22 attachments flagged. Candidates: 4, 9, 17, 28, ...

alex-ops: Rehydrate executed, restored 22 attachments from staging, verified checksums post-restore. Exit=0.

leo-eng: Quick PR opened to add checksum verification and disable optimistic-success on that codepath. Will push to canary after review.

sarah-peopleops: Thanks everyone. I'll post the recovered list and a brief impact summary to #recruiters. If this resurfaces for other imports, reopen thread. :handshake:
